t: CAD Constraint Solver - Signature build-tool concept
title: CAD Constraint Solver - Signature build-tool concept
definition: Maintains geometric relationships between model features.
description:
Every build an AI undertakes passes through CAD Constraint Solver: Maintains geometric relationships between model features. The catalog lists it among the thousand fundamental build tools because no serious building happens without it. This database is its Signature edition - the concept rebuilt as a deterministic framework with seven pillars, grounded in real techniques and standards, and taught through a ladder of runnable drills.

The Signature line treats CAD Constraint Solver as infrastructure, not inspiration. Infrastructure has contracts: given these inputs, in this state, the CAD Constraint Solver produces that output, and anyone can verify it. The seven pillars are those contracts made concrete - each owns one responsibility, each can be tested alone, and together they compose into the full capability. The technique records show the real public knowledge the pillars stand on.

Work through this database the way you would commission a machine: read the charter in the overview, inspect each pillar, check the techniques against your own knowledge, then run the drills. Every record includes a program you can execute with node - the CAD Constraint Solver is demonstrated, not merely described.

t: Signature Sketcher - CAD Constraint Solver framework pillar
title: Signature Sketcher - CAD Constraint Solver framework pillar
definition: The Sketcher component of the Signature CAD Constraint Solver framework, owning sketcher. Signature concept.
description:
The Signature CAD Constraint Solver framework decomposes the capability (Maintains geometric relationships between model features.) into seven pillars, and the Sketcher is the one that owns the framework's sketcher responsibilities. Owning a responsibility means three things in the Signature line: the pillar declares exactly what it accepts, it publishes exactly what it guarantees, and it logs enough evidence that a third party can replay its work and reach the same conclusion.

This discipline pays off when builds go wrong, because they always eventually do. When a CAD Constraint Solver result looks suspicious, the auditor does not re-run the whole build and hope; they replay the Sketcher's log, check its guarantees against its inputs, and find the fault at its source. The pillar is thus both a worker and a witness - it does the work and it testifies about the work.

Try it yourself: this record's demo runs the Sketcher's core procedure on a worked example. The program is plain JavaScript - save it as demo.js and run it with node, or press Run in the Demo Lab. Change the inputs and re-run; the procedure is deterministic, so you can verify every claim the description makes.

Signature framing: this pillar is part of the Signature line's original design for CAD Constraint Solver. It is labeled a Signature concept throughout - an engineered proposal, not an established public fact. The techniques it relies on are real and cited in the technique records of this database.

t: Signature Extruder - CAD Constraint Solver framework pillar
title: Signature Extruder - CAD Constraint Solver framework pillar
definition: The Extruder component of the Signature CAD Constraint Solver framework, owning extruder. Signature concept.
description:
The Extruder is a load-bearing component of the Signature CAD Constraint Solver framework. Its contract is narrow and absolute: within the framework, everything concerning the framework's extruder responsibilities belongs to the Extruder, and the Extruder answers for it. This separation is what makes the framework testable - the Extruder can be exercised alone, with declared inputs and checkable outputs, long before it is wired into a full build.

In operation the Extruder works like this. A build request arrives carrying the CAD Constraint Solver charter (maintains geometric relationships between model features.). The Extruder reads its portion of the charter, performs its transformation, and hands a verified intermediate result to the next pillar. If its checks fail, it stops the line and reports exactly what was wrong, instead of passing corruption downstream. That fail-fast discipline is the Signature line's signature.

Signature-concept illustration: a builder asks for a small cad job that needs CAD Constraint Solver. The Extruder takes the request's extruder responsibilities slice, applies the framework's deterministic procedure, and returns its result with a proof of what it did. Run this record's demo program to see the Extruder's core logic execute on a concrete example - the same logic, the same result, every run.

definition: The Filleter component of the Signature CAD Constraint Solver framework, owning filleter. Signature concept.
description:
Inside the Signature CAD Constraint Solver framework, the Filleter owns the framework's filleter responsibilities. Frameworks fail when responsibilities blur; the Signature line prevents that by giving each pillar a written contract, and the Filleter's contract is the sharpest of the seven. It accepts declared inputs, applies one deterministic transformation, and emits a result that any other pillar - or any auditor - can verify independently.
